A also ships no blockquote rule at all where B draws a 4px #BFBFBF bar at x=644, and A breaks its own hanging system on the quote: the '>' sits inline at 676 so the quote's first line starts at 722 while the wrap snaps back to 673.
gapTheirs: Markers are not hung: body sits at x=673 but h1 text starts at 722, h2 text at 746, bullet text at 728, ordered text at 731 — five left edges instead of one. Typing '## ' shoves the whole line 73px right; A holds every content edge at 673 and hangs the marker into the gutter (601–630), right-aligned to the column.
verdict: A gives you a prose column that never moves — '#', '##', '-', '1.' all hang out in the margin and every line of actual writing starts on the same 673px edge, so the headings read as a straight spine down the page. B indents every marked line by its own marker width, which means the left edge frays across five positions and the text physically jumps sideways the moment you promote a line to H2. B wins the caret outright — A's is text-black, 2 CSS px, and glued to the previous glyph, which is a genuine lose-your-place defect in a writing app — and B's quote rule is the only thing on either screen that makes the blockquote read as a block. But that's two fixable details against a structural flaw B commits on every marked line, and A's own quote handling is the one place it forgets its rule.

states.name: dark
states.gap: The blockquote gets no rendering at all beyond the literal '>': no rule, no indent, no tint — quote text sits at x=675 against body at 673, a 2px difference. A draws a 3px #494949 vertical rule at x=645 running the full height of the quote block, so it reads as a block from across the room; in B a two-line quote is a paragraph that happens to start with a bracket.
states.gapTheirs: Markers sit inline, not hung: the '#' starts at x=673 (same column as body text) so 'The Lighthouse' begins at 721, '## What the sea keeps' begins at 745, bullet text at 726, numbered text at 747 — four different left edges against a body column that is flush at 673. Typing '# ' shoves the whole line 48px (2 char cells) right; typing '1. ' shoves it 72px. B hangs every one of those markers into the margin (# at 625, ## at 601, - at 630, 1. at 603) so all text lands on a single 673 edge and nothing moves.
states.verdict: B is the only one of the two where the left edge of your prose is a single line. A's markers push text: heading text sits two characters right of body, ordered-list text three, so the page has a ragged staircase down the left and every line jumps sideways the instant you type the marker — the exact thing you'd notice on the fiftieth heading, not the first. A buys back some ground with the quote rule and a code chip that's actually visible (1.40:1 against the page vs B's 1.10:1), and its heading hashes are quieter (2.9:1 vs B's 4.1:1) — but it can't decide on a marker grey, running #636363 on '#'/'##' and #808080 on '-'/'1.'. Neither app scales headings: '# The Lighthouse' and '## What the sea keeps' are set at the identical 24px advance and identical weight as body, so H1 and H2 are distinguishable only by counting hashes, which is not reading at a glance.
